newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close fractionally higher.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close fractionally higher.

text.p: French stocks ended fractionally higher on Wednesday, helped by Wall Street's gains, but off their session highs as stronger-than-expected U.S. industrial production data fanned fears of higher interest rates.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished up 0.34 point, or 0.01 percent, at 2,620.97 after a seesaw session driven by Wall Street's rally on Tuesday and weakness on Wednesday morning. The CAC-40 futures contract finished down 12 at 2,614.
"Everything's being decided by what's happening in the United States," said a trader, adding investors were watching the Dow index and the dollar.
Wall Street's mid-morning recovery lifted the French market out of negative territory late in the session.

Shares in off-shore engineering company Coflexip fell 2.73 percent to 323.90 francs. CDC Bourse confirmed talk it had carried out a placement of Coflexip shares but gave no details. One fund manager said the shares were placed at 314 francs. Some dealers said re-insurer SCOR was the seller. Officials at SCOR and Coflexip declined comment.

Pen and lighter manufacturer BIC's stock rose 2.6 percent to 868 francs. On Tuesday night the company announced a 13 percent sales rise for the first quarter and proposed a two-for-one stock split for July.
Aluminium group Pechiney's shares rose 5.17 percent to 217.50 francs as investors were encouraged by the first-quarter results of its U.S. rival Reynolds Metals Co.
